posts.title: How to read a mock test result
posts.excerpt: Three numbers that matter more than the rank, with one example.
posts.content:
After every mock test, parents ask us the same thing: is this rank good enough? We look at three other numbers first. Which questions were lost to careless mistakes? Which topics were never studied? And how did the score move since last month?

A student with many careless mistakes needs calm practice under time, not more new material. A student with gaps needs those chapters before anything else. Bring the result sheet to your monthly chat and we will go through it with you, line by line.

posts.title: Why twenty minutes of homework is enough
posts.excerpt: Short, marked homework builds the habit that long evenings do not.
posts.content:
Our primary students get about twenty minutes of homework a day. Parents sometimes ask if that is too little. In our experience a short task done every day, and marked at the next lesson, does more than two hours on Sunday night.

Help by choosing one fixed time and place for it, the same every day. Do not correct it at home; let mistakes come to class, where the teacher can see what went wrong and explain it once, properly.

posts.title: Winter holiday classes: dates and groups
posts.excerpt: Six days of review in small groups, open to students from other schools.
posts.content:
Our winter classes run for six days between Christmas and the start of the new term. Each day has two eighty-minute lessons in maths and English, in groups of six, with a short test on the last day.

The classes are open to students who do not study with us during the year. It is a good way to try the school before deciding on a course. Places are limited; send us an email with your child’s school year to book.
